1:1.t:
[Passage quoted, Obad. 1.]

THE Lord God has heard a report from the Lord. And this report was about the call of the Gentiles.
1:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 5, Chapter 24

1:1.t: When I was a little child, I spoke as a little child, I understood as a little child, I thought as a little child; after I became a man, I put away the things that were a little child's. If the Apostle makes progress and, forgetting daily the things that are behind, stretches himself forward to those that are before, and, according to the precept of the Lord and Savior, holding the plough-handle, does not look back, how much more ought I, who have not yet come to the age of the perfect man and to the measure of Christ, to deserve pardon because in my youth, roused by ardor and zeal for the Scriptures, I interpreted the prophet Obadiah allegorically, though I did not know his history. My mind was burning with mystical knowledge, and because I had read that all things are possible to those who believe, I did not know that the gifts are diverse; I knew the literature of the world, and on that account I thought I could read the sealed book. […]

The vision of Obadiah. The Hebrews say that this is the man who, under Ahab king of Samaria and the most impious Jezebel, fed a hundred prophets in caves, who had not bowed the knee to Baal and were of the seven thousand whom Elijah is shown not to have known; and his tomb, together with the mausoleum of the prophet Elisha and of John the Baptist, is held in veneration to this day in Sebaste, which was once called Samaria. Herod, king of Judea, son of Antipater, called it in the Greek tongue Augusta, in honor of Augustus Caesar. Therefore, because he had nourished a hundred prophets, he received the prophetic grace, and from a leader of the army he becomes a leader of the Church. Then he had fed a little flock in Samaria; now he feeds the Church of Christ in the whole world; and φερωνύμως (true to his name), just as Stephen in the Acts of the Apostles was crowned with martyrdom, so this man too was called the servant of the Lord. […]

1:2.t: If we have learned the history, let us follow the spiritual understanding. Although you seem to yourself to be great, O heretic, and despise the fewness of the Church, yet you are small among the nations, and contemptible, and not only contemptible, but, with ἐπιτάσει (intensification), exceedingly contemptible.

There follows in the prophet Obadiah: Behold, I have given you small among the nations; you are exceedingly contemptible. The pride of your heart has lifted you up, dwelling in the clefts of the rock, exalting your throne, who say in your heart: Who will drag me down to the earth? If you are exalted like the eagle, and if you set your nest among the stars, from there I will drag you down, says the Lord. LXX: Behold, I have given you least among the nations; you are exceedingly without honor. The pride of your heart has raised you up, dwelling in the holes of the rocks, exalting your dwelling-place and saying in your heart: Who will bring me down to the earth? If you are exalted like the eagle, and if you set your nest in the midst of the stars, from there I will drag you down, says the Lord. Jeremiah, of whom we made mention above, agrees in almost the same words, saying: Behold, I have given you small among the nations: contemptible among men; […]

I said above that this very thing can also be understood against the flesh: that its powers are left without defense at the coming of Christ, and that it is contemptible and subject to the rule of the soul, and is lifted up in vain, since it dwells in the caverns of the rock, whether in the senses or in the thoughts; and it wishes to lord it over the soul, exalting its throne, and not believing that its works can be overcome. To it it is said that, however much it lifts itself up and imitates the heights of the eagle and has deceived many of the saints, yet it has been overcome and cast down by the Lord. What we have understood of the heretics and of the flesh can also be understood against the Jews.

1:3.t: The pride of your heart has lifted you up. For which of the heretics is not lifted up into pride, making little of the simplicity of the Church and reckoning faith to be want of skill? Dwelling in the clefts of the rock, exalting his throne. Although the rock is frequently put either for the person of the Lord or for solidity, whence the prophet too says: He has set my feet upon the rock, and to Peter it is said: You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, yet it is also frequently taken in the contrary sense: I will take away, he says, the heart of stone, and I will give you a heart of flesh; and: God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham; and above all here, where he did not say, dwelling upon the rock, on which the prudent builder builds his house, but in the clefts of the rock, so as to signify the cleavings of the heresies from the rock of Christ and from the Church. […]

1:4.t: [Daniel 7:4] "The first beast was like a lioness and possessed the wings of an eagle. I beheld until her wings were torn away, and she was raised upright from the ground and stood on her feet like a human being, and she was given a human heart." The kingdom of the Babylonians was not called a lion but a lioness, on account of its brutality and cruelty, or else because of its luxurious, lust-serving manner of life. For writers upon the natural history of beasts assert that lionesses are fiercer than lions, especially if they are nursing their cubs, and constantly are passionate in their desire for sexual relations. And as for the fact that she possessed eagle's wings, this indicates the pride of the all-powerful kingdom, the ruler of which declares in Isaiah: "Above the stars of heaven will I place my throne, and I shall be like unto the Most High" (Isaiah 14:14). Therefore he is told: "Though thou be borne on high like an eagle, thence will I drag thee down" (Obadiah 1:4). […]
1:4.s: St. Jerome, Commentary on Daniel, CHAPTER SEVEN

1:4.t: If, then, they are exalted like the eagle — for they too promise themselves the likeness of eagles, which are wont to gather to the Lord's carcass — and if they set their nest in the midst of the stars, from there I will drag them down, says the Lord. For just as, while the householder sleeps, the enemy sows tares over the good seed, so that great eagle, with great wings, long in the stretch of its limbs, full of feathers and of variety, which has the way of entering into Lebanon, and takes from the top of the cedar and plants it upon many waters, so that the slips may sprout into a vine, is wont to set its nest among the stars of the Church, of whom it is also said in another place: But the just shall shine like the stars.

1:5.t: Alternatively: the thieves and robbers who go out by night, because they are sons of the night and of darkness, I take to be the heretics, who preach doctrines contrary to the truth, who steal what is enough for them, and every day hasten to seize from the flocks of the Church. These, entering the vineyard of our Lord, which he brought over out of the Egypt of this world, and of whose produce he promises that he will drink wine in the kingdom of the Father, desire so to plunder everything that they scarcely leave a cluster in it.

If thieves had come in to you, if robbers by night, how would you have kept silent? Would they not have stolen what was enough for them? If grape-gatherers had come in to you, would they not at least have left you a cluster? How have they searched out Esau, tracked down his hidden things? LXX: If thieves had come in to you, or robbers by night, where would you have been cast away? Would they not have stolen what was enough for them? And if grape-gatherers had come in to you, would they not have left a cluster? How has Esau been searched through, and his hidden things been found out? Jeremiah likewise, though with the order changed: If grape-gatherers had come upon you, would they not have left a cluster? If thieves in the night, they would surely have seized what was enough for them. But I have uncovered Esau, I have revealed his hidden things, and he shall not be able to hide. […]

1:6.t: But the Lord does the contrary; for all their secrets and hidden mysteries, and those of the patriarchs of Esau — for by these I understand those who first invented heresies —, he brings into the open through his saints and through churchmen and teachers; and his first victory is that the hidden things that were covered lie open. Whence it is also said with wonder: How has Esau been searched through, have his hidden things been found out? See how Marcion and Valentinus and all the heretics, having their conscience seared, applaud themselves in doctrines of demons, and, as if initiating simple souls into certain divine mysteries, deceive them with artful speech. But when discourse has brought into the open the thirty aeons, and teams of four, and ogdoads and dodecads, and the twofold god, and the monstrous Abraxas, then the prudence of Esau will be shown to be folly, and his secrets will be tracked down.

1:7.t: They have sent you out as far as the borders, all the men of your covenant; they have mocked you; the men of your peace have prevailed against you, who eat with you; they will lay snares beneath you; there is no prudence in him. LXX: They have dismissed you as far as the borders; all the men of your testament have withstood you; your men of peace have prevailed against you; they have laid snares beneath you; there is no wisdom in him. Some divide what we expounded above, How has Esau been searched through, and his hidden things been caught?, so as to run on to 'as far as the borders', so that the sense is: your hidden things and secrets have been revealed as far as the borders. To us, however, it seems better that it be joined with what follows. […]

1:8.t: Alternatively: after those who had formerly been deceived have been converted to the Church, then, with the Lord himself doing battle, the wise of Idumea will perish, who were wise in carnal and earthly things, and prudence will be taken away from Mount Esau, the prudence which was lifted up against the knowledge of God.

Shall I not in that day, says the Lord, destroy the wise from Idumea, and prudence from Mount Esau? And your mighty ones shall fear from the South, so that the man may perish from Mount Esau. LXX: In that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the wise from Idumea, and understanding from Mount Esau. And your fighters from Theman shall tremble, so that man may be taken away from Mount Esau. When the enemy has possessed your borders, and all the men of your covenant have mocked you and prevailed against you, then wisdom will perish from Idumea, and its cunning will be shown to be folly. The Lord himself will also take away prudence from Mount Esau, that is, from the mountains of Seir, either because the city of Idumea is situated on a mountain, or because that whole region which slopes toward the south and borders on the desert is raised high with steep mountains. Hence it is also said: Your fighters from Theman shall tremble, which we have translated "south". […]

1:9.t: And those who formerly fought for Esau and Idumea with the art of dialectic, and were in the garrisons of Theman, which means consummation, will cease to fight for their former masters. Or else: those who previously promised themselves the light of knowledge, and thought that they were at noonday, will fear and be terrified, as a churchman gets the better of their sophisms, so much so that no one remains who could do battle, whether with the counsel of a king or with the strength of a fighter, for the pride of the heretics and their false doctrine.

1:10.t: Alternatively: All the things written above you shall suffer, O bloody, earthly, cruel Edom, because by a false and deadly doctrine, one that speaks impiety against God, you have slain your brother Jacob. We read in Solomon: There are those who speak and slay with the sword. And in another place: The venom of asps is under their lips, and: Their tongue is a sharp sword. Confusion therefore shall cover you, and you shall say: The confusion of my face has covered me, and you shall perish, not for a short time, but for ever. For, as far as lay in you, you struck your brother with an everlasting wound.

Because of the slaughter and the iniquity against your brother Jacob, confusion shall cover you, and you shall perish for ever. On the day when you stood against him, when strangers were capturing his army, and foreigners were entering his gates, and were casting lots upon Jerusalem, you too were as one of them. LXX: Because of the slaughter and the impiety against your brother Jacob, confusion shall cover you, and you shall be taken away for ever. From the day on which you stood against him, on the day when aliens captured his strength, and strangers entered his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, you also were as one of them. […]

1:11.t: But this too shall be a cause of torment: for when strangers were laying waste the army of Jacob and were entering through its gates into Jerusalem, once peaceful, and were casting lots in order to divide its spoils among themselves, you were one of the enemy. We read it, we have seen it, we prove it daily: when persecution arises against the Church, the Jews and the heretics become far worse persecutors of the Christians than the heathen. We can call the foreigners entering the gates of Jerusalem λογισμοὺς, that is, the most wicked thoughts, and we can interpret the gates of Jerusalem, that is, of the soul that is at rest and sees God, as the five senses, through which the enemies enter and divide the spoils of Jerusalem. If we have looked upon a woman to lust after her, death has entered through our windows. If we have taken in through our ears a lie and a judgment of blood, the enemy has entered through another gate. […]

1:12.t: Preserve, O Lord, Thy work, guard the gift which Thou hast given even to him who shrank from it. For I knew that I was not worthy to be called a bishop, because I had devoted myself to this world, but by Thy grace I am what I am. And I am indeed the least of all bishops, and the lowest in merit; yet since I too have undertaken some labour for Thy holy Church, watch over this fruit, and let not him whom when lost Thou didst call to the priesthood, to be lost when a priest. And first grant that I may know how with inmost affection to mourn with those who sin; for this is a very great virtue, since it is written: "And thou shall not rejoice over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction, and speak not proudly in the day of their trouble." Grant that so often as the sin of any one who has fallen is made known to me I may suffer with him, and not chide him proudly, but mourn and weep, so that weeping over another I may mourn for myself, saying, "Tamar hath been more righteous than I."

Alternatively: when you see your brother taken captive by various persecutions, and led away in bonds from the faith of the Church, following not his own city but whatever is foreign, you shall by no means rejoice, because you too shall suffer the like. For you rejoiced when Jacob was being captured, and over the children of Judah, whom we understand as the disciples of Christ, you exulted on the day of their destruction. And it is signified that the soul is placed midway between vices and virtues, and can be turned to either side from one hour's moment to the next. By no means, he says, shall you magnify your mouth on the day of distress. This we ought to take according to a twofold sense: of bodily distress, in persecutions and in sins; of spiritual distress, when the soul, captured by enemies and vices, has been led into Babylon.

And you shall not look down on the day of your brother, on the day of his sojourning abroad. And you shall not rejoice over the children of Judah on the day of their destruction, and you shall not magnify your mouth on the day of distress, nor shall you enter the gate of my people on the day of their ruin. LXX: And you shall not look down on the day of your brother on the day of strangers. And you shall not rejoice over the children of Judah on the day of their destruction; and you shall not speak great things on the day of distress, nor shall you enter the gates of the peoples on the day of their labors. The same sense as above: when the man has perished from Mount Esau because of the slaughter and the impiety against his brother Jacob, and everlasting confusion has covered him, he shall by no means do what he did before against his kinsman; for he shall not look down on him and think him of little account when he sees his brother going into captivity; nor shall he rejoice over the children of Judah. […]

1:13.t: Nor shall you enter the gate of my people on the day of their ruin; for when either denial or pleasure has overwhelmed us, and an unhappy conscience has not kept its former strictness, then we easily slip into contrary doctrines that flatter our error, and do not cure the wound but stroke it. It is a solace in misery for one, however lost, to have something to hope for.

Which of the heretics does not look down on the churchmen? Which does not exult in their misfortunes, if ever, because of the sins of the people, they have been handed over to persecution, and many, either of weak faith or sown upon stony ground, have fallen into denial: you may see them exult, rejoice, think our ruin their own victory, so much so that they join themselves to the nations, and the persecution becomes more savage, whether from the Jews or from those who pretend to be our brothers and are reckoned under the same name.

Nor shall you too look down on his misfortunes on the day of his devastation, and you shall not be sent out against his army on the day of his devastation.

Nor shall you stand at the exits to slay those who have fled; and you shall not shut in his remnant on the day of tribulation. LXX: And you also shall not look down on their gathering on the day of their destruction, nor shall you be added to their strength on the day of their destruction, nor shall you stand at their outlets to slay those who have been saved; nor shall you shut in their fugitives on the day of tribulation. When you yourself have been captured and destroyed by the ravaging Babylonian, among the other things that you have done, do not do these that follow. You shall not look down on, nor despise, your brother Jacob on the day of his devastation, nor shall you be added to the Babylonian army, or, you shall not be sent out against the army of Judah when, overcome by its adversaries, it has turned its back. […]

1:14.t: And when someone has slipped away, either by flight or by repentance, they stand in the byways and put forward sophisms, and bring out testimonies as if from the Scriptures, in order to offer sewn cushions to the weary and exhausted, and to put them under every elbow of the hand. And so it comes about that those who perhaps either overcame persecution by courage or escaped it through fear are, deceived by perverse doctrines, held again in the prison of errors, and this tribulation becomes far worse than that which came from the nations; for you would more easily free one captured by the heathen than one entangled in the conjuring tricks of the heretics.

1:15.t: For the day of the Lord is near upon all the nations; as you have done, so shall it be done to you. He will turn your recompense back upon your own head. For as you drank upon my holy mountain, so all the nations shall drink continually; and they shall drink and swallow up, and they shall be as though they were not. LXX: Because the day of the Lord is near upon all the nations; as you have done, so shall he do to you: your recompense shall be repaid upon your own head. Because as you drank upon my holy mountain, all the nations shall drink wine; they shall drink and swallow up, and they shall be as though they were not. And you shall cease to do these things, O Idumea, for this reason: because the vengeance of the Lord shall come upon you. For if, according to Jeremiah, those for whom there was no judgment that they should drink the cup have indeed drunk it, are you to be left as though innocent? You shall not be innocent, but you shall surely drink, as one who drinks. […]

This is Obadiah (Abdiou) the fourth in order, who also was privileged to prophesy concerning the mystery regarding Christ, and who speaks thus: Because the day of the Lord is near upon all the nations. This taken in its obvious meaning is spoken of the Scythians, that is, of Gog and Magog, but it is most properly applicable to the Lord Christ.

1:17.t: But on Mount Zion there shall be salvation, and there shall be a Holy One, and the house of Jacob shall possess those who had possessed them. And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble, and they shall be kindled among them, and shall devour them, and there shall be no remnant of the house of Esau, for the Lord has spoken. LXX: Upon Mount Zion there shall be salvation, and it shall be holy, and the house of Jacob shall possess those who had possessed them. And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, but the house of Esau stubble, and they shall be kindled against them, and shall devour them, and there shall be no grain-carrier for the house of Esau, for the Lord has spoken. When Idumea has been overthrown and devoured by the hostile nations with which it had earlier made a pact against Jacob, on Mount Zion there shall be a remnant, and there shall be salvation, and there shall be a Holy One; […]

Alternatively: When the works of the flesh have been destroyed and the earthly empire laid desolate, there shall be in the Church the salvation of those who have not gone out from their mother. And in her shall dwell the Holy One, of whom it is said in Isaiah: Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God of Sabaoth, because both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one.

And the house of Jacob the supplanter shall possess those who had possessed them as an inheritance, making Christians of persecutors, and receiving the Idumeans themselves into the faith of the Church: but the house of Esau shall be turned into stubble. And as straw cannot bear the nearness of fire, so the house of Esau shall not be able to bear the disputation of Jacob, which is set on fire by the word of the Lord: For the words of the Lord are tried by fire, nor the flame of Joseph, whose name means increase, and who, sold by his brothers, fed the people in Egypt; but at the first encounter their sophisms shall be turned to nothing. And they shall be devoured unto their own salvation, according to what is said in Isaac's blessing to Esau: But I have made him your lord; and I have subjected all your brothers to him as servants, and you shall serve your brother. […]
for the prophet shortly afterwards says: But on Mount Zion there shall be salvation.

1:18.t: And the house of Jacob, that is, of Judah, shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph, that is, of the ten tribes, a flame. For of Joseph was born Ephraim, from which tribe came the rule of Samaria; but the house of Esau, that is, of the Idumeans, who had shown themselves so savage and cruel against their brother, shall be turned into stubble. And as fire and flame swiftly devour stubble, so the two kingdoms, bound in alliance into one rod, according to Ezekiel, shall lay Idumea waste and devour it, and there shall be no one left of the people who could announce the overthrow of the adversaries to the neighboring nations. For this is what the Seventy translated πυροφόρον, which we have rendered as grain-carrier, following the idiom of the old speech; for those whom they now call agents in affairs, or post-couriers, the ancients called grain-carriers. […]

1:19.t: And those who are toward the south shall inherit Mount Esau; and those who are in the plains, the Philistines; and they shall possess the region of Ephraim and the region of Samaria; and Benjamin shall possess Gilead. LXX: And those who are in Nageb shall possess Mount Esau; and those who are in Sephela, the foreigners; and they shall possess Mount Ephraim, and the plain of Samaria, and Benjamin, and Gilead. When Judah has returned to its kingdom, Judah which dwelt in the south and possessed the whole region, according to the division made by Joshua the son of Nun, that slopes toward the Scorpion, that is, all Acrabattene, those who were formerly confined within narrow borders shall possess Mount Esau, that is, the mountains of Seir and the hill country which Edom had possessed before. […]

1:20.t: And the exile of this host of the children of Israel, all the things of the Canaanites as far as Sareptha. And the exile of Jerusalem, which is in the Bosphorus, shall possess the cities of the South. And saviors shall go up onto Mount Zion, to judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom shall be the Lord's. LXX: And this is the beginning of the exile for the children of Israel, the land of the Canaanites as far as Sareptha, and the exile of Jerusalem as far as the Euphrates; they shall possess the cities of the Nageb. And those who had been saved shall go up from Mount Zion, to punish Mount Esau, and the kingdom shall be the Lord's. In this place our translation differs greatly from the common edition; hence in the exposition of the history we must follow the Hebrew truth. Those who, according to the book of Ezra and Nehemiah, had returned from Babylon into Judea will also rightly be called the children of the exile. […]

Where we have put 'Bosphorus', the Hebrew has Sapharad, and I do not know why the Seventy could have translated it 'Ephrata', since Aquila and Symmachus and Theodotion agree with the Hebrew truth. We, however, learned from the Hebrew who instructed us in the Scriptures that the Bosphorus is so called; and, speaking as a Jew, this, he said, is the region to which Hadrian transferred the captives. When, therefore, our Christ comes, then that captivity too will return into Judea. We can, however, understand any place whatever of the kingdom of Babylon, although I also think something else. For it is the custom of the prophets, when they speak against Babylon, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Philistines and the other nations, to make use of their language in many words, and to preserve the idioms of the provinces. […]

Since we have interpreted according to the history as well as we could, and have steered our little boat among rugged rocks, let us spread the sails of spiritual understanding, so that, with the Lord breathing upon us and unlocking his mysteries, we may joyfully reach the harbor. At the time when Benjamin had possessed Gilead, the exile of the host of the children of Israel, or at any rate the beginning of the exile of the once fleshly Israel, shall be this: that it reaches the land of the Canaanites; and that the prophetic word, which was in danger of famine in Judea, once the fleece of Israel was dried up, passes over to the dew of the nations, and there is both fed and feeds, while it is both received by the believers and itself feeds the believers. Sareptha either is compounded of two words and means 'straitness of bread', or is a single word and is translated 'burning'. Canaan, on the other hand, is rendered σάλον, that is, 'motion', or else it is called 'merchant' and 'lowly'. […]

1:21.t: And when these things have been fulfilled, just as in the book of Judges the Lord would send saviors to save the people from captivity, so they shall go up and come onto Mount Zion, to judge and pass sentence on Mount Esau, that is, the Idumeans, as subject to them and serving them; and once all are subdued, the kingdom shall be the Lord's.

Now, where we have translated 'and saviors shall go up', and the Seventy rendered 'those who shall have been saved', in the Hebrew is written mosim; and these are to be understood not passively, as Aquila and the Seventy and Theodotion have it, σεσωσμένοι or ἀνασωζόμενοι (being saved), but, following Symmachus, σώζοντες, that is, actively, saviors. For σεσωσμένοι, that is, 'the saved', are called pheletim in the Hebrew tongue.

These things having thus been done, the saviors, or those who shall have been saved from the remnant of the Jewish people, shall go up onto Mount Zion, to judge and take vengeance on Mount Esau. Just as the Lord, the Light, calls his apostles light, and says: You are the light of the world; and the Rock himself granted to Peter that he should be a rock; and the good Shepherd also bestowed on them the name of shepherds, and whatever he himself is called he granted to his servants that they too should be called; so the Savior himself willed his apostles to be saviors of the world, who went up to the watchtower of the mountain of the Church and, bringing down the pride of the Jews and of all the mountains that were raised up against the knowledge of God, prepared the kingdom for the Lord.
